title: Saturday's boring SaaS, 10 October 2026
dek: Saturday, 10 October 2026. Eight are Stripe-verified. Web3Forms is Paddle-verified, and Embed Notion Pages is Lemon Squeezy.

companies.name: B2B workforce-management SaaS
companies.description: TrustMRR lists it as "B2B workforce-management SaaS" — that is the entire public description. Founded Jan 2021, bootstrapped, founder "david" (~256 X followers). Stealth (no public homepage / domain). Stack on the public profile: Stripe backend only. Audience: B2B. Pricing model: "Try for free" (founder-stated).
companies.evidence: ~$243,487 MRR (−3.1% L30), 2,505 active subscriptions, ~$75,029 L30 (−71.6%; snapshot ~$76,174), ~$599,951 last 3 months, ~$1,441,053 last 6 months, ~$3,028,974 last 12 months, ~$9,301,725 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~07:45 Warsaw (05:45 UTC). Not listed for sale.
companies.indieAngle: Pick one WFM wedge for PL/EU deskless niches that still live in Excel + WhatsApp — cleaning crews, facility maintenance, or restaurant multi-site — and sell schedule + timesheet + simple compliance docs at €8–€15/seat. Don't try to out-build UKG; own one vertical's onboarding and payroll-export formats.
companies.whyItPrints: Workforce management is the textbook boring vertical — schedules, time tracking, compliance paperwork for deskless teams. ~$243k MRR with 2,505 seats implies a mid-market / SMB seat product that compounds for years (my inference from MRR ÷ subs ≈ $97/mo average — my calculation). L30 cash is lumpy (−71.6%) while MRR is almost flat (−3.1%), which is what multi-year / annual SaaS often looks like on a 30-day cash window.

companies.name: Web3Forms
companies.description: A no-backend contact-form API: drop an HTML form on a static site and submissions land in email / webhooks without PHP or a server (company-stated). Founded Dec 2020, IN. Founder Surjith S M. Free forever (250 submissions/mo); paid for higher limits. Stack: Next.js, Tailwind, Vercel, Hetzner, Cloudflare, Paddle. DR 85.
companies.evidence: ~$41,988 MRR (+7.2% L30), 3,038 active subscriptions, ~$44,688 L30 (+0.4%), ~$133,499 last 3 months, ~$250,351 last 6 months, ~$318,476 all-time (L12 = AT on this profile), ~95% L30 profit margin. Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~06:26 Warsaw (04:26 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Same product for EU privacy-sensitive static sites (Astro/Hugo on Cloudflare Pages): EU-hosted inbox, GDPR DPA, spam scoring, and a Zapier/Make + Notion/Sheets destination pack sold as "Form API for EU agencies" at €19–€49/mo.
companies.whyItPrints: Contact forms are the original developer glue. ~3,038 subscriptions at ~$42k MRR with a 95% L30 profit margin is the dream indie shape: tiny infrastructure, SEO/docs-led acquisition, and a free tier that converts when a site gets real traffic. L30 is flat (+0.4%); MRR up +7.2%.

companies.name: Capgo
companies.description: Live updates / OTA for CapacitorJS apps — ship JS/CSS fixes without waiting for App Store review, plus channels, rollback, native builds, and release automation (company-stated). Founded Nov 2021, EE. Team 2–5, bootstrapped. Founder Martin Donadieu. ~7,800 estimated users (founder-stated). SOC 2 Type II / SOC 3 / ISO 27001 (founder-stated). Stack: Astro, Vue, Supabase, Cloudflare, Resend, Stripe. DR 59.
companies.evidence: ~$32,254 MRR (+6.8% L30), 1,167 active subscriptions, ~$33,650 L30 (−10.7%; snapshot ~$33,773), ~$101,893 last 3 months, ~$177,989 last 6 months, ~$289,169 last 12 months, ~$555,048 all-time, ~38,047 L30 visitors, ~$0.89 revenue/visitor, ~47% L30 profit margin. Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~04:06 Warsaw (02:06 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: If Capacitor is crowded, do the same OTA + channel + rollback story for Expo/React Native shops that refuse full Expo EAS, or sell a "hotfix channel" managed service for agencies that ship 10+ client apps and hate store review roulette.
companies.whyItPrints: App Store review delay is a permanent tax on mobile teams. Capgo sells the missing "CodePush for Capacitor" wedge — devops glue, not a consumer AI app. ~1,167 subs at ~$32k MRR with ~47% L30 margin and ~38k L30 visitors is a real B2B tools business. MRR growing +6.8% even while L30 cash is −10.7%.

companies.name: Supliful
companies.description: Private-label CPG dropshipping for creators — supplements, coffee, skincare, pet products — with product selection, e-commerce enablement, and fulfillment in one platform; no inventory to manage (company-stated). Founded Jun 2017, US. Founder Martins Lasmanis. Free to design; selling from $69/mo ($55/mo annual). ~1.6M estimated users (founder-stated). Domain: supliful.com, DR 71.
companies.evidence: ~$179,949 MRR (−1.5% L30), 3,341 active subscriptions, ~$990,628 L30 (−0.7%; snapshot ~$991,205), ~$2,964,734 last 3 months, ~$5,972,387 last 6 months, ~$11,526,994 last 12 months, ~$53,654,567 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~05:47 Warsaw (03:47 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Don't compete on US supplements. Build a narrow EU private-label lane (PL/DE food supplements or pet treats) with one 3PL, Shopify + Stripe Tax, and a €79/mo "brand + fulfillment" seat for indie creators who already have an audience.
companies.whyItPrints: This is fulfillment + white-label ops packaged as SaaS. L30 cash (~$991k) ≫ MRR (~$180k) because they also charge when end-customers buy products (platform take / product revenue flowing through Stripe — my inference from founder description "We charge customers at the time they make the purchase"). Nine figures all-time on TrustMRR. Boring physical-goods glue with software margins on the SaaS layer.

companies.name: Online language learning platform
companies.description: "Profitable online language learning platform combining live 1-on-1 tutoring with AI-powered speaking practice, personalized learning and learner analytics" (TrustMRR / founder-stated). Tutor marketplace + subscriptions + proprietary AI practice. Founded Sep 2021, US. Team 11–25, bootstrapped. ~35,000 estimated users; "thousands of tutors and over 1M lessons analyzed" (founder-stated). Stack: React, React Native, Laravel, Python, Stripe. Listed for sale at $7,500,000 (1.1x; first listed Sep 16, 2026; 5 offers; ~2,767 recent viewers).
companies.evidence: ~$147,528 MRR (+8.5% L30), 655 active subscriptions, ~$591,565 L30 (+2.8%; snapshot ~$592,670), ~$1,513,978 last 3 months, ~$2,438,329 last 6 months, ~$4,442,894 last 12 months, ~$8,040,035 all-time, ~482,105 L30 visitors, ~$1.23 revenue/visitor, ~21% L30 profit margin. Asking $7,500,000 (1.1x). Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~08:29 Warsaw (06:29 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Don't buy a $7.5M tutor marketplace. Clone the wedge for one language pair with expensive B2B buyers (PL↔DE corporate language training, or PL nurses → DE/NO medical German) sold as company seats, not consumer freemium.
companies.whyItPrints: Language tutoring marketplaces are an old model; the AI speaking layer is garnish on a human-supply business that already invoices monthly. L30 cash (~$592k) is ~4× the listed MRR (~$148k) — seller message says reported MRR understates cash (nearly 5×; founder-stated). Big, real, and for sale at a low multiple if the diligence holds.

companies.name: Lookup product
companies.description: TrustMRR value proposition is literally "Lookup product." Utilities category, $18/month pricing, solo founder (Alptekin Can), founded Jun 2026, AE. No public domain. Listed for sale at $1,400,000 (3.0x Growth tier; first listed Oct 9, 2026; 1 offer; ~213 recent viewers).
companies.evidence: ~$25,489 MRR (−70.4% L30 MRR growth snapshot), 2,107 active subscriptions, ~$39,051 L30 (+157.6%; snapshot ~$39,171), ~$61,643 last 3 months, ~$63,761 all-time (L6/L12 = AT), ~95% L30 profit margin. Asking $1,400,000 (3.0x). Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~08:58 Warsaw (06:58 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Build a named EU registry lookup — CEIDG/KRS company cards, UDT certificates, or vehicle history for PL/CZ/SK — sold as $9–$19/mo API + web UI. Same shape as Plate Lookup / 1Lookup, localized.
companies.whyItPrints: "Lookup" businesses (VIN, plate, phone, company registry, certificate status) are pure query-API cash machines — high margin, SEO/ads acquisition, almost no support. This one is only ~4 months old with ~95% L30 margin, ~2,107 subs at $18/mo, and L30 cash up +158%. Caveat: MRR growth snapshot is −70.4% (likely a short history / plan-mix artifact on a young listing — my inference); treat diligence as mandatory before the $1.4M ask.

companies.name: MyCater
companies.description: B2B catering marketplace for French companies — breakfast, lunch, corporate events, cocktail receptions — with curated caterers, ordering, invoicing, and support for HR / EAs / office managers (company-stated). Founded Nov 2020, FR. Team 2–5, bootstrapped. ~1,000 estimated users; 5-star rated (founder-stated). Stack: TypeScript/JS, Cloudflare, MySQL, Node.js, RabbitMQ, Sentry, Stripe. Channels: newsletter, SEO. DR 39.
companies.evidence: ~$0 MRR, 0 active subscriptions, ~$70,610 L30 (+98.1%), ~$131,203 last 3 months, ~$288,968 last 6 months, ~$618,329 last 12 months, ~$2,449,537 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~05:40 Warsaw (03:40 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Warsaw / Kraków office-lunch marketplace with 20 vetted caterers, company invoicing (NIP / Faktura), and a Slack/Teams "order lunch for Thursday" bot. Charge caterers 12–15% take-rate; don't build a consumer food app.
companies.whyItPrints: Office catering is a weekly recurring ops headache. $0 seat MRR with ~$70.6k L30 (+98%) and ~$2.45M all-time means take-rate / order GMV through Stripe, not SaaS seats — classic marketplace boring. Same lane as MyTraiteur (covered Oct 7) but this is the buyer-side B2B marketplace, not a quote tool.

companies.name: Indexsy
companies.description: Operator-led SEO, content, and link-building services sold as packaged products — AuditStack $50, local guest posts from $90, niche edits from $95, "LLM Booster" from $99, local PBN citations from $250, BrowserBlast from $250 (company-stated). Founded Dec 2015, CA. Founder Jacky Chou. Domain indexsy.com, DR 65.
companies.evidence: ~$44,506 MRR (−17.6% L30), 28 active subscriptions, ~$87,749 L30 (−19.4%; snapshot ~$88,204), ~$304,144 last 3 months, ~$613,728 last 6 months, ~$989,445 last 12 months, ~$2,689,990 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~04:02 Warsaw (02:02 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Productize one SEO SKU for PL/EU SaaS — "ChatGPT / AI Overview citation pack" (the Indexsy "LLM Booster" wedge) sold as a €499 audit + €1.5k/mo content retainer. Don't rebuild a full agency; sell one measurable outcome.
companies.whyItPrints: SEO services with a productized price list is the original boring internet business. 28 subscriptions at ~$44.5k MRR implies ~$1.6k/mo average retainer (my calculation) — high-ticket, not self-serve freemium. L30 cash (~$88k) > MRR because a chunk is one-time audits / link orders. Eleven years in; ~$2.7M all-time.

companies.name: Fast Corp Ltd.
companies.description: Fully online Bulgarian company formation + accounting / compliance desk — company ready in 3–5 business days, 10% corporate tax pitch, EU IBAN & banking support (company-stated). Founded (TrustMRR profile), BG. Team 2–5. ~3,000 estimated users. Channels: Facebook, Instagram, Google Ads, Meta Ads, partnerships. Domain fastcorp.eu (DR 4).
companies.evidence: ~$0 MRR, 0 active subscriptions, ~$8,645 L30 (0.0% growth on snapshot), ~$56,373 all-time, ~70% L30 profit margin. Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~07:57 Warsaw (05:57 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: "Polish LTD / Estonian OÜ / Bulgarian EOOD in a box" comparison funnel for indie SaaS founders who want an EU company + VAT + Stripe, sold as a €799 formation package + €99/mo bookkeeping. Partner with one local accountant; own the SEO for "open EU company as non-resident."
companies.whyItPrints: Cross-border company formation is bureaucracy glue — same lane as Get Brazil Visa / Easy Moving Permits / P7M.io. $0 MRR with ~$8.6k L30 and ~70% L30 margin means one-time formation packages (+ maybe bookkeeping upsells) rather than seats. Ads-heavy acquisition on a low-DR domain; the product is the process, not the brand.

companies.name: Embed Notion Pages
companies.description: Embed public Notion pages into WordPress, Webflow, or any site without coding; content stays synced. Paid plans add password/email gates, custom CSS, bulk imports, API (company-stated). Founded Aug 2022, NL. Founder Ozan van Oosten-Şener. Free / Pro $10/mo ($96/yr, 20 embeds) / Unbound $35/mo. Stack: React, Tailwind, TypeScript, Cloudflare, Lemon Squeezy, SendGrid, Supabase. DR 45. Listed for sale at $29,900 (2.2x Starter; first listed Oct 9, 2026; 0 offers; ~264 recent viewers).
companies.evidence: ~$1,318 MRR (−9.4% L30), 102 active subscriptions, ~$1,112 L30 (+5.3%), ~$3,130 last 3 months, ~$7,225 last 6 months, ~$17,626 last 12 months, ~$40,942 all-time, ~89% L30 profit margin. Asking $29,900 (2.2x). Owner-reported extras on profile: ~$1,067 Lemon Squeezy net last month; ~$77 opex; ~$990 cash profit before tax/owner pay (founder-stated). Revenue synced Oct 10, 2026 ~08:58 Warsaw (06:58 UTC).
companies.indieAngle: Buy it — or clone the "gated Notion docs for client portals" wedge for agencies (password + email allowlist + custom domain) and sell Unbound-style seats to consultancies that refuse to migrate off Notion.
companies.whyItPrints: Classic CMS-bridge glue. Notion's native embeds hurt growth (founder notes revenue −24% over the past year) but the paid customization / access-control layer still pays ~$1.3k MRR at ~89% margin with almost no ongoing work (founder-stated). Perfect micro-acquisition for someone who wants a quiet cash-flow app.
